title: pd-disaggregation: fold the TPU guide into the main guide, cache TPU weights on the node, pin TPU7x to vllm-tpu v0.26.0
body:
## Summary

Folds the separate TPU page of the P/D disaggregation guide into the main guide, and fixes two problems found while validating the TPU7x path end to end.

Three commits, each independently revertable:

1. **Fold the TPU guide into the main guide.** `README.tpu.md` was last synced with the shared content on 2026-06-12 and had drifted (dead benchmark anchor, retired `run_only.sh` flow, an env block that sourced `env.sh` before `REPO_ROOT` was set, an unflagged inheritance of the H200-calibrated `peakPrefillThroughput`). It is replaced by a `#### TPU` section next to `#### GPU`, with the dynamic sub-slicing content reduced to a pointer at `docs/infrastructure/providers/gke/dynamic-slicing/`. `README.tpu.md` and the orphaned `benchmark-templates/tpu.yaml` are deleted. The model-server overlays stay where they are; the nightly TPU workflow selects them by `accelerator_type`, and the other CI jobs discover work by path, so no CI change is needed.
2. **Cache model weights on the node for the TPU overlays.** Adds the node-local HuggingFace cache (`hostPath /var/cache/huggingface`, `HF_HOME`) already used by the GKE GPU overlays to the TPU base patches and the dynamic-slice manifests. Without it every container restart re-downloaded the 406 GB TPU7x model into the writable layer, which triggered ephemeral-storage eviction on nodes with other data on the boot disk. The boot-disk requirement is documented.
3. **Pin the TPU7x overlays to `vllm-tpu:v0.26.0`.** In `v0.27.0` through `v0.29.0` the vLLM scheduler reads `connector._kv_transfer_config` (`requires_kv_delivery`), but the bundled `TPUConnectorHMA` skips the base-class initializer, so EngineCore fails at startup with `AttributeError: 'TPUConnectorHMA' object has no attribute '_kv_transfer_config'`. Fixed upstream by vllm-project/tpu-inference#3566 (2026-09-12); no `vllm-tpu` release contains it yet. The shared `tpu-vllm/release` component stays at `v0.27.0` because tiered-prefix-cache's TPU multi-host offload (#2313) needs it; a new `tpu-vllm/release-v0.26.0` component pins only the two HMA overlays. The v6e overlay uses the non-HMA `TPUConnector` and is unaffected. This commit is reverted once a release includes the fix.

## Validation

* Deployed `modelserver/tpu/v7/vllm` from this branch on GKE TPU7x (`2x2x1`, 1 prefill + 1 decode, standalone router). `/v1/completions` and `/v1/chat/completions` succeed through the EPP; the prefill engine logs the KV send and the decode engine the KV pull for every request; decode reports 100% external prefix-cache hits (574/574 prompt tokens over three requests).
* Every `kustomization.yaml` under `guides/pd-disaggregation` builds; `tpu/v6/vllm` renders `v0.27.0`, both TPU7x overlays render `v0.26.0`.
* `make verify`, markdownlint (no new findings beyond the existing `<h4>`-in-`<summary>` pattern), yamllint, and the router `helm template` pass.
* Internal links and anchors in the changed Markdown resolve.

## Note

The regression in commit 3 was not caught by CI because the nightly TPU lane only runs `tpu/v6`. A TPU7x lane for the HMA path would close that gap after we can get capacity for nightly e2e test.

cc: @achandrasekar @ahg-g

title: fix(pd-disaggregation): add shared HF cache to vLLM CoreWeave overlay
body:
Motivation:
The vLLM CoreWeave overlay was missing the shared HuggingFace cache and
Xet-disable settings that the GKE overlay for this guide already has,
leaving CoreWeave pods without a shared model cache across restarts and
exposed to Xet CDN 429s when multiple pods pull the model at once.

Approach:
Add JSON6902 patches to
guides/pd-disaggregation/modelserver/gpu/vllm/coreweave/kustomization.yaml,
matching this file's existing `op: add` patch style, for both the decode
and prefill Deployments:
- HF_HOME, HF_HUB_DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT, and HF_HUB_DISABLE_XET env vars
- a volumeMount at /root/.cache/huggingface
- a node-local hostPath volume (huggingface-cache) backed by
  /var/cache/huggingface

title: fix(pd-disaggregation): drop the ROCM_ATTN backend pin from the AMD overlay
body:
The AMD NIXL P/D nightly has failed since 8/18, when the guide moved to `llm-d-rocm:v0.9.0`. Its vLLM 0.26.0 base rejects the `ROCM_ATTN` attention backend whenever a KV connector is configured, causing every prefill and decode pod to exit at startup:

```
ValueError: Selected backend AttentionBackendEnum.ROCM_ATTN is not valid for this configuration. Reason: ['KV connector not supported']
```

The overlay pinned the backend for heterogeneous TP transfer, but now vLLM sets the KV cache layout that the NIXL connector needs on its own and only auto-selects backends that pass the KV connector check, so the pin is removed from prefill and decode.

The nightly itself can verify this working now. Previous failure traceback from the [9/22 run](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/actions/runs/35682014366).

Context: #2523

title: feat(wide-ep-lws): add Qwen3-235B Intel XPU deployment guide
body:
Add an Intel XPU deployment for aggregated `Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B` serving using
vLLM, in the WideEP guide with TP8 per node and EP16 spanning 16 XPUs across two nodes.

## Topology

This configuration deploys Qwen3-235B with **EP16 across two nodes**:

| Setting | Value |
|---|---:|
| Nodes / LWS pods | 2 |
| XPUs per node | 8 |
| Total XPUs | 16 |
| Tensor parallel size | 8 |
| Data parallel size | 2 |
| Expert parallel size | 16 |
| RDMA NICs per node | 1 |

Each node runs one vLLM instance using TP8 across its eight local XPUs.
The two instances form DP2 across the two nodes. With expert parallelism
enabled, the model's experts are distributed across all 16 XPU ranks,
forming an **EP16 cross-node topology**.

```text
                       llm-d Router / EPP
                               |
                        Service port 8200
                               |
              +----------------+----------------+
              |                                 |
          Node 0 / LWS leader              Node 1 / LWS worker
          DP rank 0                        DP rank 1
          TP8: XPU 0-7                     TP8: XPU 8-15
          1 RDMA NIC                       1 RDMA NIC
              |                                 |
              +------ EP16 over XCCL/OFI -------+
                    allgather_reducescatter
```

Intel XPUs and RDMA network devices are allocated through Kubernetes
DRA using the gpu.intel.com and dranet-rdma DeviceClasses.

Changes
- Add the Qwen3-235B LeaderWorkerSet model server manifests.
- Configure vLLM with TP=8, DP=2, FP8 quantization, and expert
parallelism.
- Configure XCCL over OFI verbs for cross-node communication.
- Add DRA claims for eight Intel XPUs and one RDMA NIC per pod.
- Add an aggregated-serving EPP configuration targeting port 8200.
- Document the commands required to deploy the Qwen3-235B model and
its router configuration.
- Assign stable qwen-0 and qwen-1 hostnames to avoid ambiguous
hostname-prefix matching during oneCCL local-rank discovery.

title: fix(sglang): align P/D KV-page size with EPP chunking and sibling guides
body:
## What this changes

Adds `--page-size=64` to SGLang prefill and decode deployments in `guides/pd-disaggregation/`.

SGLang defaults to `page_size=1` (token-level KV allocation). In this guide, the llm-d EPP router configures `approx-prefix-cache-producer`, which tracks prefix caching in 64-token chunks. Aligning SGLang's KV-page size to 64 prevents conservative under-counting of prefix hits by EPP, and aligns this guide with the other SGLang guides in the repository (`tiered-prefix-cache`, `precise-prefix-cache-routing`).

Also updates `aws/patch-prefill.yaml` to repeat the flag, because that patch restates the full `args` list and strategic-merge replaces lists.

## Testing

Verified manifest rendering across all overlays:

```bash
for o in base aws coreweave gke; do
  kubectl kustomize guides/pd-disaggregation/modelserver/gpu/sglang/$o | grep -E -- '--page-size=64'
done
```

All overlays render `--page-size=64` on both prefill and decode deployments.

title: docs(autoscaling): deprecate WVA and pin its image to release-0.9
body:
## What

WVA is deprecated and gets no further releases — `v0.9.0` is the final version (upstream also carries a `wva-engine-eol` tag). This pins the WVA guide assets to that release and marks the path deprecated.

### Image pin

The controller overlays already tracked `?ref=release-0.9`, but the image tag came from whatever the upstream overlay happened to set. Both platform overlays now pin it explicitly:

```yaml
images:
  - name: ghcr.io/llm-d/llm-d-workload-variant-autoscaler
    newTag: v0.9.0
```

`kustomize build` on `wva/controller/platform/{k8s,ocp}` renders `…llm-d-workload-variant-autoscaler:v0.9.0`.

### Deprecation notices

- **`guides/workload-autoscaling/README.md`** — warning at the top pointing new deployments at the KEDA + EPP paths, naming Saturation-based Autoscaling as the closest replacement for WVA's saturation signal. `KEDA + WVA Metrics (Legacy)` → `(Deprecated)`.
- **`wva/README.md`** — replaces the stale VariantAutoscaling warning (it said the CRD "will be removed in 0.9.0", already past) with the deprecation notice, keeping the CRD fact as context.
- **`replica-rebalancing/README.md`** — deprecation folded into the existing experimental-feature blockquote, since the rebalancer ships inside WVA.

### Workflows

The three WVA nightly lanes each built the controller **from `main`** and passed it via `WVA_TAG`, which the deploy scripts turn into an `images:` override — that would have defeated the pin. For `nightly-e2e-workload-autoscaling-{ibm-acc-gpu,cks-acc-gpu,amd-acc-rocm}-vllm-x.yaml`:

- Removed the `build-wva-image` job; `nightly` no longer `needs:` it.
- `WVA_TAG` now comes only from the optional `image_tag` dispatch input, so the overlay pin applies by default.
- `caller_ref` default `main` → `release-0.9`, so the e2e suite matches the image.
- Schedules disabled on cks (07:30 UTC) and amd (13:00 UTC); ibm's was already off and its reason is updated. All three keep `workflow_dispatch`.

`nightly-e2e-workload-autoscaling-keda-epp-ibm-acc-gpu-vllm-x.yaml` is EPP-only and untouched.

## Testing

- `kustomize build` on both platform overlays renders `v0.9.0`.
- `make verify-guide-readmes` passes.
- `markdownlint-cli2` error count on the three READMEs unchanged from base (all pre-existing).
- All three workflows parse and no longer contain `build-wva-image`; no dangling references remain.

## Notes for reviewers

- `permissions: packages: write` was left in place on the three workflows — now unused for pushing, but reusable workflows inherit permissions and I did not want to risk an image pull.
- The three `consolidate-status-workload-autoscaling-{amd,cks,ibm}` badge workflows and the WVA badge in the guide README still exist. With schedules off those badges will go stale, so retiring them may be worth a follow-up.

title: fix(wide-ep): make Intel XPU decode manifest actually cross-node wide-EP
body:
## Problem

`decode.yaml` shipped with `leaderWorkerTemplate.size: 1` and only a `workerTemplate` (no `leaderTemplate`). Every "decode" pod was a fully independent TP+EP-only replica — no pod ever shared a DP/EP group with another pod. Despite the guide's name, expert parallelism was never actually organized across pods/nodes on the Intel XPU path.

## Fix

* `decode.yaml`: split into `leaderTemplate` (HTTP API + routing-proxy sidecar, DP-supervisor rank 0) and `workerTemplate` (`--headless`, exec-based probes). `leaderWorkerTemplate.size` bumped `1 -> 2` (smallest config that exercises real cross-pod EP). `vllm serve` args rewritten to the DP-supervisor pattern. Added `podAntiAffinity` (leader/workers on distinct hosts, scoped to this guide) and `rolloutStrategy` (avoids surge-based rollout deadlocks on capacity-constrained clusters).
* `prefill.yaml`: added the same `podAntiAffinity`/`rolloutStrategy`. `size` stays `1` — prefill scales via independent replicas, not a cross-node EP group; its own wide-EP is unvalidated and documented as such inline.
* `kustomization.yaml`: added a labels-transformer path for the new `leaderTemplate`.
* `router/xpu.values.yaml`: EPP endpoint selection now also requires `leaderworkerset.sigs.k8s.io/worker-index: "0"`, since headless decode workers share every other label with the leader but don't serve HTTP on port 8000.
* `README.md`: updated the Intel XPU config table and added notes on the fix and current EPLB status.

## Validation

Validated on a real 4-node/16-XPU Intel cluster: EP world size > 1 actually spans pods, correct expert split, cross-node P/D traffic (NIXL), and light concurrent request handling.

EPLB (expert-parallel load balancing) was not enabled as part of this fix; it's left as follow-up work for Intel XPU.

## Known gaps

* EPLB unsupported/unvalidated on Intel XPU (follow-up work).
* Not tested behind a Gateway/InferencePool front-end (direct Service routing only).
* Only tested with the small `DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat` model, light concurrency only.
* `guides/wide-ep/monitoring` still assumes GPU-style `rank0..rank7` ports; pre-existing gap, not touched here.
* Prefill's own cross-node wide-EP (vs. replica scale-out) is unvalidated and out of scope.

title: fix(ci): default harness_resources to 2/8Gi for Intel XPU nightly workflows
body:
## Problem
3 Intel XPU nightly workflows have been failing every run since 2026-09-09:
- `nightly-e2e-optimized-baseline-intel-acc-xpu-vllm-x`
- `nightly-e2e-pd-disaggregation-intel-acc-xpu-vllm-x`
- `nightly-e2e-precise-prefix-cache-routing-intel-acc-xpu-vllm-x`

```
Failed to deploy pod 'inference-perf-xxx': The Pod "inference-perf-xxx" is invalid:
spec.containers[0].resources.requests: Invalid value: "64Gi": must be less than or equal to memory limit of 8Gi
```

## Cause
- These workflows send `harness_resources=32/64Gi` to `llm-d-infra`'s reusable workflow, which only overrides the harness pod's memory **request** (`--set harness.resources.memory=64Gi`).
- Since `llm-d-benchmark#1882` (merged 2026-09-08), the memory **limit** comes from a separate field, `harness.resources.memoryLimit`, hard-coded to `8Gi` in the `intel-xpu` overlay used by these 3 scenarios.
- Result: `requests.memory=64Gi > limits.memory=8Gi` → Kubernetes rejects the pod → no harness pod → run fails.

## Fix
Default `harness_resources` to `2/8Gi` for these 3 workflows, matching the intel-xpu overlay's `memoryLimit`. This isn't an arbitrary downgrade — it's the value the overlay was originally sized for (single-node Kind/B60, harness sharing the node with the serving stack), and it ran successfully for weeks before `harness_resources` was introduced (see 8/18–8/27 run history, all green).

Other (non-XPU) nightly workflows are untouched — their overlays use the global default `memoryLimit=128Gi`, so `32/64Gi` doesn't conflict there. `predicted-latency-routing` / `wide-ep-lws` / `tiered-prefix-cache` on Intel XPU are also untouched — they don't set `accelerator.profile: auto`, so this overlay/bug doesn't apply to them.

## Scope
Stopgap only. Filing a follow-up issue on `llm-d/llm-d-infra` to also override `memoryLimit` alongside `memory`, so this can't recur for other accelerator overlays.

fix(workload-autoscaling): capture WVA controller diagnostics before CKS teardown
body:
Motivation:
The nightly CKS workload-autoscaling lane
(workload-autoscaling-cks-acc-gpu-vllm-x) has failed for at least seven
consecutive nights waiting for wva-controller-manager to become
Available. The root cause is unknown because the controller pod is
force-deleted during teardown before its state can be inspected —
kubectl describe output and pod logs never make it into the run output.

Approach:
Wrap the `kubectl wait deployment/wva-controller-manager ... --for=condition=Available`
step in nightly-deploy-cks.sh so that on failure, before the script exits
(and before the calling workflow tears the namespace down), it captures
and prints to stderr:
  - `kubectl describe` of the Deployment
  - `kubectl describe`, `kubectl logs --all-containers`, and
    `kubectl logs --all-containers --previous` (to catch a crashed prior
    container instance, e.g. CrashLoopBackOff) for every pod matching the
    wva-controller-manager- name prefix
This mirrors the existing diagnostics block later in the same script
(the KEDA fallback check), so it matches this file's own conventions.
nightly-deploy-ocp.sh's `kubectl wait` step does not have an equivalent
failure-diagnostics wrapper today — that parity gap is left for a
follow-up, since this PR only targets the CKS nightly lane the issue is
about. The script still exits 1 on failure, preserving the original CI
failure semantics.

This does not fix the underlying reason the controller never becomes
Available — that root cause is still unconfirmed and requires
inspecting a live CKS run. This change implements next step #1 from
the issue report ("Capture kubectl describe deploy/wva-controller-manager
plus the controller pod's events and logs before teardown runs") so the
next nightly failure leaves enough evidence in the run log to diagnose
the real problem.

Validation:
No live CKS/GPU cluster is available in this environment, so the
underlying Available-timeout failure itself could not be reproduced or
confirmed fixed (it isn't meant to be fixed by this change). What was
run:
  - `bash -n guides/workload-autoscaling/scripts/nightly-deploy-cks.sh` — passed.
  - `shellcheck -x --severity=warning guides/workload-autoscaling/scripts/nightly-deploy-cks.sh` — zero warnings.
    (Note: this repo's .pre-commit-config.yaml only runs the shellcheck
    hook against docker/scripts/*.sh, so this script is not gated by
    that hook; ran shellcheck manually as an extra check.)
  - Extracted the new diagnostic block into an isolated harness with a
    stubbed `kubectl` simulating the exact failure mode from the issue
    (kubectl wait returns 1, one matching pod
    wva-controller-manager-6bfcf4cfb5-qxvkw as in the issue's log
    excerpt). Confirmed: describe/logs/logs --previous output print in
    the correct order for the deployment and the matching pod, the
    pod-name grep matches correctly and is empty-safe under pipefail,
    and the script still exits 1, preserving the original failure path
    for the caller.

Report: https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/issues/2124
Signed-off-by: Pujitha Paladugu <10557236+pujitha24@users.noreply.github.com>
Assisted-by: claude-sonnet-5 (via Claude Code)

Fixes #2124

title: docs(operations): add OrcaRouter as an external LLM provider in the LiteLLM guide
body:
## Summary

Add a named **OrcaRouter** external LLM provider to the LiteLLM "Serve External APIs" guide, mirroring the existing Google Gemini external provider pattern.

[OrcaRouter](https://www.orcarouter.ai) is an OpenAI-compatible gateway that smart-routes `orcarouter/auto` to an appropriate upstream model. It also runs gateway-level, zero-trust security for AI agents on the same endpoint — screening every prompt/response and governing every tool call on a default-deny basis, with no application code changes.

## What changed

- `docs/operations/serve-external-apis/litellm.md`
  - **Step 1 (Secrets)**: added `ORCAROUTER_API_KEY` export and `litellm-env` secret literal.
  - **Step 3 (`model_list`)**: added a named `orcarouter-auto` entry:
    ```yaml
    - model_name: orcarouter-auto
      litellm_params:
        model: openai/orcarouter/auto
        api_base: https://api.orcarouter.ai/v1
        api_key: os.environ/ORCAROUTER_API_KEY
    ```
  - **Step 4 (Verify)**: updated `/v1/models`, `/key/generate`, the inference example (new subsection C), and `/key/info` to cover `orcarouter-auto`.
- `docs/operations/serve-external-apis/README.md`
  - Added OrcaRouter to the section intro and the architecture diagram.

## Validation

- `markdownlint` (repo `.markdownlint.json`) — clean.
- `check-yaml` / `check-json` / `trailing-whitespace` / EOF / mixed-line-ending (pre-commit hooks) — clean.
- YAML `model_list` block parses with all four entries intact.
- Live connectivity: `POST https://api.orcarouter.ai/v1/chat/completions` with model `orcarouter/auto` returned **HTTP 200** (`ORCA-LIVE-OK`, finish `stop`).

No code or cluster behavior is changed; this is a docs-only addition.

Disclosure: I'm an engineer on the OrcaRouter team.

title: Fix stale forward-looking version claims in WVA guides for 0.9.0
body:
Fixes #2357

`guides/workload-autoscaling/wva/README.md` and
`docs/architecture/advanced/autoscaling/hpa-wva.md` described the 0.9.0 release in future tense even though they ship inside the 0.9.0 tag itself:

- "The VariantAutoscaling CRD will be removed in 0.9.0",  but the CRD was already removed as of 0.9.0 (confirmed against
  llm-d-workload-variant-autoscaler release-0.9, which no longer ships
  a CRD manifest).
- "Saturation engine v2 will be the default in the next release (0.9.0), but for now it must be enabled manually", but v2 is
  already the default as of 0.9.0 (confirmed via the shipped saturation ConfigMap, which already includes the `analyzers:`
  section that selects v2).
  
A reader on the v0.9.0 tag had no way to tell from the docs whether these "future" events had already happened.

title: Set UCX_IB_ROCE_REACHABILITY_MODE=all in the wide-ep GKE overlay
body:
Two things found while running wide-ep as a DisaggregatedSet on a GKE A4 (B200) cluster with GKE managed DRANET.

- GKE puts each of the eight RDMA NICs on its own subnet. UCX's default reachability check rejects the remote RoCE v2 GID across subnets and falls back to the link-local GID, so the NIXL transfer fails. `UCX_IB_ROCE_REACHABILITY_MODE=all` fixes prevents this. The pd-disaggregation GKE overlays already has this so adding it to the wide-ep GKE overlay too.
- Hybrid Mamba models (GLM-5.3-Flash) need `VLLM_SSM_CONV_STATE_LAYOUT=DS` or the NIXL connector refuses to start. No wide-ep manifest serves such a model today, so this is a README note only.

Tested that prefill to decode transfers over RDMA succeed in both DisaggSet ordinal and hash group identity modes.

title: Aggregated wide-ep GLM 5.3 flash guide with gke overlay
body:
**(Stacked ontop of https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/pull/2555, see latest commit for diff)**

Add an aggregated (non-disaggregated) wide expert parallelism modelserver
overlay (`guides/wide-ep/modelserver/gpu/vllm-glm-5.3-flash-aggregated/`)
for serving `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` (`Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration`,
320B total / 18B active parameters, 288 routed experts) across 2 x 8-GPU
nodes (16 x NVIDIA B200 GPUs).

Key details:
- Configure `LeaderWorkerSet` (`size: 2`) with `DP=16, EP=16, TP=1`
  (18 routed experts per GPU) using vLLM's DP Supervisor on port 8008
  (`--data-parallel-multi-port-external-lb`, ports 8000-8007) and
  `--reasoning-parser glm47` / `--tool-call-parser glm47`.
- Use the `gpu-vllm/nightly` component (`v0.29.1rc1+`) required for the
  `glm5_next` hybrid KDA linear attention + sparse NoPE MLA architecture
  and TileLang mHC / DSA kernels.
- Set `TRITON_LIBCUDA_PATH=/usr/local/nvidia/lib64` and `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`
  so Triton/FLA kernels locate GKE's mounted `libcuda.so.1` in Ubuntu-based
  upstream `vllm-openai` images.
- Use `--all2all-backend allgather_reducescatter` over GKE DRANET RoCEv2
  RDMA NICs (`gke-rdma-nic-template`, `mrdma.google.com` `gpu0rdma0`-`gpu7rdma0`)
  to avoid the unpatched NVSHMEM `ibv_create_ah` issue on GKE COS.
- Document `GLM-5.3-Flash` deployment and architecture sizing in
  `guides/wide-ep/README.aggregated.md` and `gke/README.md`.

title: Update multimodal guides to use leaf name for ci/cd testing
body:
## What does this PR do?

Re-submission of #2556 (authored by @rlakhtakia — commit authorship and sign-off preserved via cherry-pick) with the merge conflict against `main` resolved. That PR's head branch is the fork's `main`, which we don't have push access to update.

Original description from #2556:

> CI/CD was failing because of multimodal nested directory. llm-d-benchmark and llm-d-infra have been updated to now use leaf name of guide. This change updates multimodal guide to use the leaf name for testing.

Everything else is the original commit as-is, including its whitespace/EOF lint fixes.

## Checklist

- [x] Code follows project contributing guidelines
- [ ] Tests pass locally (`make test`)

title: fix(e-disaggregation): drop placeholder image from e-pd encode patch
body:
## What does this PR do?

Removes the explicit `image: REPLACE_MODEL_SERVER_IMAGE` line from `guides/multimodal-serving/e-disaggregation/modelserver/gpu/vllm/e-pd/base/patch-encode.yaml`.

## Why is this change needed?

The GKE e-disaggregation nightly fails with encode pods stuck in `InvalidImageName`:

```
spec.containers[modelserver]: Failed to apply default image tag "REPLACE_MODEL_SERVER_IMAGE": couldn't parse image name ...
```

Root cause is kustomize transformer ordering. In `e-pd/base/kustomization.yaml`, the encode skeleton comes from `recipes/modelserver/base/single-host/e-pd` and is filled in by `patch-encode.yaml`. Kustomize applies **component** transformers before the kustomization's own **patches**, so the `images/gpu-vllm/ec-connector` component substitutes the placeholder first, and the explicit `image:` field in `patch-encode.yaml` then overwrites it back to `REPLACE_MODEL_SERVER_IMAGE`. Decode is unaffected because `patch-decode.yaml` carries no `image:` field, and e-p-d is unaffected because it ships encode as a full resource (substituted by the component, never re-patched).

With the image line removed, the encode container keeps the component-substituted image.

## How was this tested?

- [ ] Unit tests added/updated
- [ ] Integration/e2e tests added/updated
- [x] Manual testing performed

`kubectl kustomize` on all four overlays before/after:

| Overlay | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `e-pd/base`, `e-pd/gke` | encode = `REPLACE_MODEL_SERVER_IMAGE` | encode = `ghcr.io/llm-d/vllm-openai:ec-cpu-connector-support` |
| `e-p-d/base`, `e-p-d/gke` | unchanged | unchanged |

Also verified the rendered encode Deployment still carries the full patched spec (command/args, ports `modelserver`+`ec-nixl`, `nvidia.com/gpu: 2`, probes, volumes).

## Checklist

- [x] Commits are signed off (`git commit -s`) per DCO
- [x] Code follows project contributing guidelines
- [x] Linters pass locally (rendered with `kubectl kustomize`)
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)

title: fix(ci): unpin SGLang tiered cache nightly cluster

## What

Drop `cluster_name` and `cluster_zone` from the SGLang tiered-prefix-cache
nightly lane so it uses the llm-d-infra default, `llm-d-e2e-us-east5`. This is a follow-up PR for https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/pull/2480

## Why

The lane was pinned to `llm-d-e2e-us-south1-2`, which no longer has any GPU
nodes. Its `a3u-dra-pool` is gone and only `default-pool` and `pool-1` remain,

```
decode.acceleratorType.labelValue

```

Because nothing is deployed at that point, the run also logs a misleading
`namespaces "..." not found` while collecting debug information.

The pin was never needed. This lane serves Qwen3-32B at TP=2 and requests
`nvidia.com/gpu` directly, with no DRA or RDMA, so it belongs on the reserved
H100 cluster alongside the optimized-baseline SGLang lane and both vLLM
tiered-prefix-cache lanes, none of which set `cluster_name`. `us-east5` has a
16-node `h100-pool` and already carries the vLLM tiered lane at 4 replicas x 2
GPUs, so it has room for this lane's 2 x 2.

## Testing

Confirmed the lane passes only `cluster_namespace`, matching the other H100
lanes, and that yamllint is clean:


title: Add COMPONENTS.md: core and ecosystem component roles
body:
## What

Adds `COMPONENTS.md`, defining two classes of component the project maintains:

- **Core** - on the inference request path; a failure or regression there
  degrades or breaks live inference. Deliberately small, carries production
  reliability expectations.
- **Ecosystem** - maintained and first-class, but not needed to serve a
  request (planning, benchmarking, analysis, simulation, adjacent services).

The role is orthogonal to graduation: a component moves from
`llm-d-incubation` into the main `llm-d` org and takes on one of the two roles
at that point. An ecosystem component can later be promoted to core if it moves
onto the request path and meets the higher bar.

## Why

Today "in the main org" is a single undifferentiated signal with no written
graduation criteria, so every graduation becomes an argument. This gives
committed-but-off-path components (starting with `llm-d-planner`) a real home
without implying request-path guarantees, while keeping the core set small and
high-bar to protect the request path.

## Notes

- Graduation criteria are grounded in the existing principles in `PROJECT.md`
- Includes a starter roster. The roster is the source of truth and changes by
  pull request.

title: fix(ci): wait for flow-control request bursts
body:
The flow-control validator launches background request bursts inside command substitutions, so their PIDs cannot reliably be waited on by the parent shell. The final metrics scrape can run before requests finish and report misleading flow-control configuration failures.

Start each band in the parent shell and capture its PID with `$!`. Wait for every band, including when an earlier band fails. Before evaluating metrics, check each band's process exit status and require the expected number of HTTP 2xx responses. Failed or incomplete bursts print their logs and stop validation before configuration assertions. These diagnostics run in the existing nightly validator.

Validation:
- Six temporary local shell scenarios cover concurrent success, failures in the premium and standard processes, HTTP 500, HTTP 302, and missing responses.
- Every scenario waits for all three bands before cleanup; request failures stop before flow-control metric assertions.
- `bash -n`, `shellcheck`, applicable changed-file pre-commit hooks, and `git diff --check` pass.

Local validation used temporary fixtures outside the repository. No live Kubernetes E2E run was performed.

Validation:

- Direct shell checks cover HTTP error, execution error, missing JSON object, and success diagnostics.

fix(guides): unify PROVIDER_NAME default to none
body:
`guides/optimized-baseline` and `guides/modelexpress-p2p` documented different defaults for `PROVIDER_NAME`, the value passed to `--set provider.name=` in the router gateway install. PR #2260 changed the optimized-baseline README default to `none` inside the rendered `guide:env.static` block. Both `guide.yaml` files, the render source of truth, still said `gke`, so `scripts/guide.py render` would have reverted the README.

Both guides default `PROVIDER_NAME` to `none`, matching the router chart's default for `provider.name`. GKE users must set `PROVIDER_NAME=gke`: with `none`, the chart omits the `HealthCheckPolicy`, the load balancer health check fails against vLLM, and requests return 503. Each `guide.yaml` carries a comment above the variable stating the requirement, and each README states it in prose above the env block.

Related fixes in the same files:

- optimized-baseline `guide.yaml` declares `ROUTER_CHART_VERSION`. The variable existed only in the README's rendered block, so `guide.py render` deleted it and `render --check` failed on `main`.
- `guides/recipes/router/README.md` documented `provider.name=<gke|istio|none>`. The placeholder lists all four accepted values, and a paragraph describes what each value renders.

Seven other guide READMEs export `PROVIDER_NAME=gke` without a warning; a follow-up issue should track that sweep.

**Verification:**

- `scripts/guide.py check` and `scripts/guide.py render --check` pass for both guides.
- The scheduled GKE nightlies for both guides use `gateway_class: epponly` (standalone mode), which does not read `PROVIDER_NAME`, so the default change does not affect CI.

Fixes #2330

title: feat(sglang): add tiered prefix cache GKE nightly lane
body:
## Summary

Add the nightly E2E workflow and status consolidation job for SGLang tiered prefix cache CPU offloading on GKE GPU, closing the remaining automated-testing gap for SGLang alongside `optimized-baseline` and `pd-disaggregation`.

The lane resolves to `guides/tiered-prefix-cache/modelserver/gpu/sglang/native/cpu/gke` (`offloading_target: cpu`, `connector: native`). L3 / filesystem offloading is **not** added to CI here.

## Overlay fixes required for CI execution

Two defects in the `cpu` overlay prevented `llm-d-infra` from standing it up:

- **Model auto-detection.** `llm-d-infra` derives the served model by stripping the `--model-path=` prefix and discarding anything still shaped like a flag. Bare option values on their own list items (`write_through`, `kernel`) survive that filter, so detection returned 3 lines instead of 1 and the result was passed on as `--model`. Normalizing to `--flag=value` restores single-line detection.
- **`decode_pods` override.** Renaming `base/patch-sglang.yaml` to `base/patch-decode.yaml` lets `llm-d-infra`'s glob (`patch-{vllm,decode}.yaml`) apply the functional-gate override. Without it the lane would stand up the guide's benchmark topology of 8 replicas at TP=2.

## Memory sizing

Raise decode container memory `limits` from `400Gi` to `512Gi` and `requests` from `200Gi` to `400Gi`. `--hicache-size` is **per TP rank**, so `200` at TP=2 pins ~372.5 GiB of host memory; together with the `20Gi` memory-backed `/dev/shm` volume charged to the same cgroup, a `400Gi` limit left no room for Python and CUDA runtime allocations.

## Scope note: the `fs` overlay

The `fs` overlay is **not exercised by this lane**. It is fixed here because it carries the identical model-detection defect (5 bare values rather than 3) and would fail the moment CI is pointed at it. That change is limited to the argument form plus one wrong field name in a comment — no behavioural change.

## Workflow scheduling and isolation

Runs at `18:30 UTC` daily, 3 hours after P/D SGLang on the same cluster, with status consolidation at `20:30 UTC`. Dedicated namespace, Helm release (`llmdbenchcicdr-gke-sglang-tiered`), and runner workspace directory (`/tmp/llmdbenchcicdk-gke-sglang-tiered`) so runs do not collide with sibling GKE lanes.

## Testing

Replayed `llm-d-infra`'s model detection pipeline against all four `sglang` overlays — each now returns exactly one line (`Qwen/Qwen3-32B`), where `cpu/gke` previously returned 3 and `fs/gke` 5:

```bash
kubectl kustomize <overlay> \
  | yq .spec.template.spec.containers[0].args \
  | sed 's^--model-path=^^g' \
  | grep -Ev "\- \--|\- '|\---|\- \||    \--|.*exec vllm|'|null|#|\"|find|START_RANK" \
  | sed -e 's^ ^^g' -e 's|^-||g' -e 's^\\^^g' -e '/^$/d' | uniq
```

Rendering, lint, and matrix sync:

```bash
kubectl kustomize guides/tiered-prefix-cache/modelserver/gpu/sglang/native/cpu/gke
kubectl kustomize guides/tiered-prefix-cache/modelserver/gpu/sglang/native/fs/gke
pre-commit run --files \
  .github/workflows/nightly-e2e-tiered-prefix-cache-gke-cpu-gpu-sglang-native.yaml \
  .github/workflows/consolidate-status-tiered-prefix-cache-gke-cpu-gpu-sglang-native.yaml \
  guides/tiered-prefix-cache/modelserver/gpu/sglang/base/kustomization.yaml \
  guides/tiered-prefix-cache/modelserver/gpu/sglang/base/patch-decode.yaml \
  guides/tiered-prefix-cache/modelserver/gpu/sglang/native/cpu/base/patch-sglang.yaml \
  guides/tiered-prefix-cache/modelserver/gpu/sglang/native/fs/base/patch-sglang.yaml
touch .release-team && python3 scripts/sync-nightly-matrix.py --check && rm -f .release-team
```

> [!NOTE]
> `scripts/sync-nightly-matrix.py --check` also fails on a clean `main` checkout — the `wide-ep-lws` AMD MoRIIO workflow was added without regenerating `release/README.md`. That drift is pre-existing and deliberately left out of this PR; `release/README.md` here changes only the row for this lane.

title: fix(interactive-pod): respect namespace for gateway lookup
body:
run-guide-llm.sh queried the Gateway without a namespace. When the interactive pod ran outside the default namespace, kubectl could not find the Gateway, and the benchmark then proceeded with an empty address instead of reporting the cause.

Pass the injected NAMESPACE to kubectl, enable strict shell error handling, and fail explicitly when the Gateway has no assigned address.

title: fix(makefile): restore the leading tab on the uninstall-docker completion message
body:
`Makefile:213` starts at column zero, so make does not read it as part of the `uninstall-docker` recipe.

The line contains a colon, in `Remove alias if set:`, so make reads it as a rule rather than reporting a missing separator. The file parses with no warning.

## Two consequences

The recipe ends at line 212, so the completion message never prints:

```
$ make -n uninstall-docker | tail -1
docker stop llm-d-container && docker rm llm-d-container
```

`install-docker` at `:205`, `uninstall-k8s` at `:243` and `uninstall-openshift` at `:272` all print theirs. This is the only one that does not.

And make defines a target out of the text:

```
$ make -p -n | grep '^@echo'
@echo: unalias llm-d"
```

## After

```
$ make -n uninstall-docker | tail -1
echo "docker uninstallation complete. Remove alias if set: unalias llm-d"

$ make -p -n | grep -c '^@echo'
0
```

## The repository already states the rule

`.editorconfig`, added in #2103:

```
# Makefiles require tabs
[Makefile]
indent_style = tab
```

## Scope

One character. A scan of the whole file for a column-zero line inside a recipe block returns line 213 and nothing else. The only other hits were `:302` to `:311`, the space-indented prerequisite continuation under `check-tools`, which is correct as written.

`make uninstall-docker` was run with `-n` only. Running it for real stops and removes a container.

## Duplicate search

`gh issue list --state all` for `Makefile tab` and for `uninstall-docker`, and `gh pr list --state all` for `Makefile`, return nothing covering this.

Open PR #2339 edits this same line, to swap `$(PROJECT_NAME)` for `$(IMAGE_REGISTRY_REPO)`, and keeps the column-zero start. It is `CONFLICTING` today. If it lands first the tab still needs adding, and if this lands first that PR needs a one-line rebase.

title: Added recipe for inference cost
body:
This PR is the same as https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/pull/1926 except that it doesn't update the existing guides to support cost.

This PR implements an llm-d guide to deploy inference cost tracking capabilities for llm-d.
Implements the first phase of [this proposal](https://github.com/simanadler/llm-d/blob/5c5bd7c5981ea155a9059787a63ec0ec728d409e/docs/proposals/inference-costs.md)

OpenCost is used to provide the cost metrics and APIs, and the guide describes how to deploy these capabilities in a cluster to get the costs associated with the models run via llm-d.

The related https://github.com/opencost/opencost/pull/3845 has been merged by the OpenCost maintainers.

 NO changes are made to files in other guides to align model name labels for accurate cost tracking.

The keda-epp-token-aware guide invokes calibrate.sh directly, but the script was tracked with mode 100644. Guide execution therefore failed with Permission denied and exit code 126 before calibration could run.

Mark calibrate.sh as executable with mode 100755 so the guide can invoke it directly without changing the script contents.

title: fix(build): remove invalid buildx command prefix
body:
The Docker branch of the buildah-build recipe runs as one continued shell block, so the leading '-' before docker buildx create was passed to the shell as a command name instead of acting as a Make error-ignore prefix. The existing || true hid that error, and docker buildx use image-builder then failed in a clean environment because the builder was never created.

Remove the invalid '-' while retaining || true, allowing the buildx create command to run and preserving the existing tolerance for an already-existing builder.

Tests:
- make -n buildah-build BUILDER=docker
- git diff --check
- Verified the generated recipe contains docker buildx create followed by docker buildx use without the invalid command prefix.

title: feat(guides): serve encode disaggregation on the vLLM nightly image
body:
## Summary

Move the Coordinator Disaggregation guide and the multimodal Encode Disaggregation
guide (E/PD and E/P/D) from pinned development vLLM images to the upstream vLLM
nightly image. Configure the
[ECCPU Connector](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/features/ec_cpu_connector/) in its
P2P NIXL mode, with the V2 model runner that it requires. In the Coordinator guide,
replace the Coordinator's CPU render sidecar with a Service that fronts the prefill
model servers. Add CoreWeave overlays for E/PD and E/P/D. Make the vLLM model
servers and the Coordinator pull their moving image tags (`:nightly`, `:main`) on
every start.

The nightly pin is temporary: we expect to move to the vLLM 0.29.0 release image
once it ships, since encoder-cache transfer is not in any released version yet.

## Changes

### Both guides: vLLM nightly image and ECCPU Connector

- **Image:** the `gpu-vllm/nightly` component (`docker.io/vllm/vllm-openai:nightly`)
  replaces `ghcr.io/revit13/vllm-openai:61e53561a` (Coordinator guide) and the
  `gpu-vllm/ec-connector` component (`ghcr.io/llm-d/vllm-openai:ec-cpu-connector-support`,
  Encode Disaggregation guide). The component already adds the `USER=llm-d`
  workaround for vllm-project/vllm#44548, so the inline copies are removed.
- **`imagePullPolicy: Always`:** the `gpu-vllm/nightly` component now sets it on the
  vLLM container. `:nightly` moves every day, and with `IfNotPresent` a node that
  cached an older nightly runs a different vLLM build. In a live E/PD test, one encode
  pod ran vLLM 0.28.1 from a cached image while the other pods ran 0.29.1. The EC
  connector compatibility check includes the vLLM version.
- **`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`:** set only on instances that have
  `--ec-transfer-config`, because `ECCPUConnector` raises `ValueError` without the V2
  model runner:
  - Coordinator guide: encode, prefill
  - E/P/D: encode, prefill
  - E/PD: encode, decode
- **EC config:** P2P NIXL mode (`"ec_enable_nixl": true`). `ec_cpu_bytes`, which is
  required and has no default, replaces `num_ec_blocks`. The sizes keep the earlier
  capacity (Qwen3-VL-32B uses 40,960 bytes per encoder token):

  | Instances | Before | `ec_cpu_bytes` | Blocks | `/dev/shm` |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | E/P/D encode, E/P/D prefill, E/PD encode | `num_ec_blocks: 1000000` | 40 GiB | 1,048,576 | 90Gi |
  | E/PD decode | default (100,000) | 4 GiB | 104,857 | 20Gi |
  | Coordinator encode, prefill | default (100,000) | 4 GiB | 104,857 | 8Gi |

- **Docs:** each `--ec-transfer-config` has a comment that links to
  https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/features/ec_cpu_connector/.

### Coordinator Disaggregation guide

- **`--enable-scale-out` on all model servers:** `vllm serve` serves `/render`,
  `/derender` and `/inference/v1/generate` only with this flag
  (vllm-project/vllm#55176 replaced `VLLM_ENABLE_SCALE_OUT_ENDPOINTS` with it).
  Prefill needs it for render. All roles need it because the Coordinator sends
  `/inference/v1/generate` to every phase for `/inference/v1/generate`, Responses
  and Messages requests.
- **Render Service (`render/`, new):** render (`/v1/*/render`) is CPU-only work in
  the vLLM API server, so any vLLM instance that serves the model can handle it.
  Before this change, all render calls went to one `vllm launch render` sidecar in
  the Coordinator pod. llm-d/llm-d-router#2701 (fixes llm-d/llm-d-router#2696) adds
  render balancing across discovered endpoints, but only for the EPP
  `token-producer`. The Coordinator's `render` step still takes one `address`. So
  this guide spreads the render load with a Service: `coord-disaggregation-render`
  fronts the prefill pods on their `modelserver` port, and render capacity grows
  with the prefill replicas. The render step address is
  `http://coord-disaggregation-render.${NAMESPACE}.svc:8000`. The `.svc` suffix
  matches `NO_PROXY` in `multimedia-downloader/patch-coordinator-ca.yaml`, so render
  calls do not go through the media proxy.
  - Prefill only, not all vLLM pods: render on decode slows token streaming.
    Encode sets no `--max-model-len`, so render there accepts prompts that prefill
    and decode reject. Prefill returns one token per request, so its API server has
    spare CPU.
  - The `vllm-render` sidecar (`vllm-openai-cpu:v0.26.0`) and its volumes are
    removed. Render now runs on the same vLLM version as the model servers, and no
    extra copy of the model is downloaded.
- **Coordinator image:** `ghcr.io/llm-d/llm-d-router-coordinator:main` now uses
  `imagePullPolicy: Always`, because `:main` moves with every merge to llm-d-router
  main.
- **README:** step 2 applies `render/`, Cleanup deletes it, and the image note
  describes the nightly image and the EC settings.

### Encode Disaggregation guide

- **CoreWeave overlays (new):** `e-pd/coreweave` and `e-p-d/coreweave` add
  `rdma/ib: "1"` to each role. `rdma/ib` is removed from the E/P/D base decode and
  prefill patches, so the base and GKE overlays no longer request it. The README
  lists `coreweave` as a provider.
- **README:** describes the nightly image, the V2 model runner and the P2P NIXL
  settings. The GKE bullet no longer claims DRA and DRANet (RoCE), because the GKE
  overlays do not configure RDMA yet.

## Defaults

- `--enable-scale-out`: off in `vllm serve` when not set. Set only in the
  Coordinator guide. The multimodal guides do not use the scale-out endpoints and
  keep the default. vLLM builds from before 2026-09-14 do not know the flag.
- `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER`: not set on decode in the Coordinator guide and in
  E/P/D. vLLM then uses V2 by default (vllm-project/vllm#53183) and falls back to V1
  when a feature needs it.
- `ec_cpu_bytes`: required, with no default. vLLM does not check it against the
  `/dev/shm` size, so each value is below its pod's `/dev/shm` limit.
- `imagePullPolicy`: Kubernetes uses `IfNotPresent` when it is not set and the tag is
  not `:latest`. It is now `Always` on the vLLM container in every guide that uses
  `gpu-vllm/nightly` (E/PD decode and wide-EP GLM-5.2 already set it) and on the
  Coordinator.
- Render step `address`: no default in the Coordinator. It is now the Service URL.

## Testing

- [x] `kustomize build` passes for the Coordinator model servers (`base`,
  `coreweave`, `gke`), `coordinator/` and `render/`, and for E/PD and E/P/D
  (`base`, `coreweave`, `gke`). All 38 kustomizations that use `gpu-vllm/nightly`
  build, and the only change there is `imagePullPolicy: Always`.
- [x] Checked the built manifests. Every Deployment uses
  `docker.io/vllm/vllm-openai:nightly`. No env var name is duplicated. The V2 runner
  is set only on EC instances. The render Service selects only prefill pods. The
  render address host matches `NO_PROXY`.
- [x] Deployed E/P/D on CoreWeave and sent an image request. The encode pod logged
  `EC save`, `serving NIXL READ request` and `NIXL READ completed`, and prefill
  answered. A text-only request skipped encode.
- [x] Deployed E/PD on CoreWeave and sent an image request. The encode pod logged
  `NIXL READ completed`, and decode answered.
- [x] Deployed the Coordinator guide on CoreWeave (3 EPPs) and sent a text and an
  image request through the Gateway. Render went through `coord-disaggregation-render`
  to a prefill pod (`/v1/chat/completions/render` 200, 83 tokens, 1 image), and the
  encode pod logged `NIXL READ completed`. Both requests returned 200.

## Notes

- The Service balances connections, not requests. For more render capacity, add
  prefill replicas or CPU. llm-d/llm-d-router#2701 balances render per request, but
  only in the EPP. If the Coordinator's `render` step gets a similar option, it can
  replace this Service.
- The `ec_cpu_bytes` sizes depend on the model. For another model, calculate
  `out_hidden_size * (1 + deepstack layers) * dtype bytes` per token.
- GKE RDMA: the E/PD, E/P/D and Coordinator GKE overlays do not configure RDMA yet,
  so the NIXL KV-cache and encoder-cache transfers use TCP on GKE. We will open a
  follow-up issue to add the `gke-rdma` DRA component (one GPU+NIC claim per TP rank),
  as in the P/D Disaggregation guide, once it can be tested on a GKE A3/A4 cluster
  with DRA and DRANet.

body:
## Summary

The TPU PodMonitor added in #2190 provides a scrape recipe, but llm-d has no dashboard for inspecting the collected hardware metrics. This PR adds a GKE TPU overview dashboard and documentation for enabling it and diagnosing missing data.

- Show exporter scrape health, TensorCore utilization, HBM bandwidth utilization, and runtime duty-cycle and memory gauges when available.
- Reuse the shared dashboard loader and `${DS_PROMETHEUS}` convention. The dashboard selects a single exporter job using an exact match and filters hardware metrics with `make="cloud-tpu"`. It preserves per-instance and per-accelerator series instead of aggregating them. Panels show `No data` when a metric is unavailable.
- Document metric names, units, label scope, availability checks, and compatibility limits in the TPU recipe and observability reference.

The metric names and labels are based on the GKE device-plugin metrics consumed by [Ray's TPU metrics parser](https://github.com/ray-project/ray/blob/be4889928d3a396d7a1476d1bac3288dac72f9ab/python/ray/dashboard/modules/reporter/reporter_agent.py). The utilization metrics and their `make="cloud-tpu"` labels also appear in a [GKE v6e sample shared in a Ray issue](https://github.com/ray-project/ray/issues/57829).

ICI, PCIe, VPU, and kube-state-metrics topology recording rules remain follow-up work.

Relates to #2157

## Validation

- `make verify` passed.
- Markdown lint, JSON parsing, local documentation links, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Local Prometheus 3.5.0 `promtool` checks passed: 34 dashboard query cases and six label-isolation cases using synthetic data. Coverage includes missing metrics, scrape failures, multiple instances, other component jobs, and foreign/missing `make` labels.
- As a negative control, replacing the exact job matcher with a regex matcher caused the label-isolation checks to fail.

The query checks were run locally; this PR adds no test tooling or CI dependencies. No live GKE/TPU deployment validation was available. The synthetic checks validate query behavior, not hardware metric availability.

title: Add remaining-work routing variant to the P2P KV-cache-sharing guide [Experimental]
body:
Adds a variant guide under `guides/p2p-kv-cache-sharing/remaining-work-routing/`, linked from the parent P2P guide's variant sections.

The variant routes long-context follow-ups by their remaining prefill work instead of their total length: a request whose prefix is pullable over the P2P tier counts only its fresh tail, so it runs on a short-work prefill class and pulls the prefix instead of queueing behind cold long prefills. Prefill classes split by the `llm-d.ai/prefill-work-range` label; the boundary is derived from deployment measurements (peak per-rank prefill throughput plus the pull cost model) by the included `calibrate_work_boundary.py`, which also emits the labels and EPP parameters as one consistent set.

Contents: deploy manifests (GLM-5.2-FP8, 3x DP8 engines), router configuration for the baseline and remaining-work EPPs (one-parameter difference), the calibration script, the benchmark harness, and measured results on agentic traces (C64: migration-eligible TTFT p50 -53%, and -33% on top of an engine-side `--long-prefill-token-threshold` baseline).

Marked [Experimental]: the EPP side depends on llm-d-router#2559 (issue llm-d-router#2540), still in review, and the split-pool premise is scale-dependent - at two prefill engines an undivided pool with prefix-affinity scoring can outperform the split; the guide targets deployments that require work-class separation.

Relates to: llm-d-router#2540, llm-d-router#2559.

title: Fix: Wrong URL to Download Latest GAIE Manifests
body:
`guides/env.sh`  defines  `GAIE_URL`  to generate the correct download path:

```
export GAIE_VERSION=${GAIE_VERSION:-latest}
if [[ $GAIE_VERSION == "latest" ]]; then
  export GAIE_URL=releases/latest/download
else
  export GAIE_URL=releases/download/${GAIE_VERSION}
fi
```

Download URLs should therefore use  `GAIE_URL` . Otherwise, when  `GAIE_VERSION`  defaults to  latest , the following URL is invalid and returns HTTP 404:

```
https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api-inference-extension/releases/download/${GAIE_VERSION}/v1-manifests.yaml
```

The correct version-aware URL is:

```
https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api-inference-extension/${GAIE_URL}/v1-manifests.yaml
```

title: fix(smoke-test): keep the real /v1/models status in the summary table
body:
`check_models` discards the status it has just reported. `helpers/smoke-test/healthcheck.sh:184` fails with the real code, and `:185` overwrites it with `000`, which is the sentinel `curl` produces when nothing answered at all.

So a reachable endpoint returning 503 reads as unreachable in the summary table, while the failure list directly below it shows the true code. Both come from the same variable in the same run:

```
║  /health          HTTP 503               ║
║  /v1/models       HTTP 000   count=-     ║
║  /v1/chat/completions HTTP 503   8     ms   ║
...
Failures:
  - /v1/models returned HTTP 503
  - /v1/chat/completions returned HTTP 503
```

`/health` and `/v1/chat/completions` both report 503 correctly. `/v1/models` is the outlier.

Every other exit from this code keeps the status: `check_health` at `:171`, and `check_models` itself at `:194` and `:210`. This is the only path that loses it.

## The change

Reporting `${http_code}` covers both cases, because `curl` already yields `000` when the connection fails. Verified against a 503 server and against a port nothing listens on:

```
=== 503 server ===
║  /v1/models       HTTP 503   count=-     ║
=== nothing listening ===
║  /v1/models       HTTP 000   count=-     ║
```

The sentinel survives where it is real, and the true code survives where there is one.

## Test

`tests/test_healthcheck_failure.py` already stands up a `ThreadingHTTPServer` answering 503 to everything, but asserted only the exit code, the `UNHEALTHY` banner and the word `failed`. It now also asserts the row.

```
$ python -m pytest helpers/smoke-test/tests/
1 passed

$ shellcheck -x --severity=warning helpers/smoke-test/healthcheck.sh
(exit 0)
```

Revert the script, keep the test, and it fails on the new assertion.

## Not checked

`report_json` at `:373` reads the same `MODELS_RESULT` and is affected identically, but this run did not exercise `-o json`.

## Duplicate search

`gh issue list --state all` and `gh pr list --state all` over `healthcheck.sh`, `smoke-test healthcheck` and `v1/models HTTP 000` return only #2401, which fixed the subshell counter accounting in this same file and merged on 2026-08-30, and #767, the original addition. Nothing covers this.

title: docs(autoscaling): make KEDA + EPP the architecture path, deprecate WVA
body:
## What

Audit of `docs/architecture/advanced/autoscaling/`. The folder presented WVA as a co-equal path and — in the VA migration section — as the recommended one. WVA is deprecated, so the folder now leads with KEDA + EPP and keeps WVA as a design reference.

## Renames

The loop is KEDA-owned rather than a hand-written HPA, so the `hpa-` prefixes were misleading:

| Old | New |
|---|---|
| `hpa-epp.md` | `keda-epp.md` |
| `hpa-wva.md` | `wva.md` |
| `hpa-architecture.svg` | `keda-epp-architecture.svg` |

All inbound references updated (`docs/menu-config.json`, the folder README, `docs/architecture/README.md`). The SVG was orphaned *and* drew the deprecated Prometheus Adapter chain; it is redrawn as EPP → Prometheus ← KEDA → KEDA-owned HPA, and is now actually referenced from the doc.

## Content

**`keda-epp.md`** covered only the queue signal. It now carries a signal table spanning the four deployable paths — queue depth, pool saturation, token backlog, estimated latency — with their EPP metrics and guides, plus the `scalingModifiers` pipeline step the SLO-aware path needs and the limitation the path actually has: no cost-aware choice of hardware.

Two things it does *not* lack, both previously miscredited to WVA alone:

- **Pending pods.** A trigger is a PromQL query, so it can read replica counts from kube-state-metrics. The SLO-aware `ScaledObject` does exactly that, discounting its ask by `readyReplicas/replicas` so a scale-up in flight does not race to `maxReplicas`.
- **A contended accelerator budget.** Kueue gates replica pods against per-model quota floors *below* the HPA, so it composes with any of the signals and leaves KEDA sole owner of the HPA it generates.

**`wva.md`** gains a whole-doc deprecation warning and a *Migrating off WVA* section (pick a signal → delete WVA-managed HPAs/VA objects **before** creating the `ScaledObject`, since two HPAs on one Deployment conflict → uninstall the controller). Its pre-existing VA→HPA+WVA migration is marked historical rather than recommended.

**`README.md`** is restructured: KEDA + EPP first with the four-signal table, WVA in past tense under a warning, and the old "Features Matrix" reframed as *What Changed with the Deprecation* — the capability gaps, not a menu of equals.

**Also:** `slo-aware-keda.md` gains a line placing it as a specialization of `keda-epp.md` (its content was accurate, unchanged otherwise); `docs/architecture/README.md`'s "two complementary approaches" paragraph rewritten; `menu-config.json` re-keyed with all three docs ordered and labeled.

## Note for reviewers

Three links point at `guides/workload-autoscaling/kueue-rebalancing/README.md`, which lands with #2458 and **does not resolve until that merges.** Either merge #2458 first, or say so and I will drop the links and keep the prose.

Not touched, as it is outside the folder: `guides/workload-autoscaling/README.md` still labels WVA "(Legacy)" rather than deprecated, and its observability table still leads with WVA metrics — worth a follow-up if the guides should match.

All other relative links and anchors in the folder verified resolving; `menu-config.json` re-parsed as valid JSON.

title: docs(wide-ep-lws): order Intel XPU modelserver command before NVIDIA GPU
body:
## What / Why

The nightly **Wide EP LWS E2E (Intel XPU)** workflow started failing on 2026-09-16 (e.g. https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/actions/runs/35169787515/job/105038823569) with:

```
Model server deploy failed: error: must build at directory: not a valid directory:
evalsymlink failure on '.../guides/wide-ep-lws/modelserver/xpu/vllm-deepseek-r1-0528/':
lstat ...: no such file or directory
```

`modelserver/xpu/vllm-deepseek-r1-0528/` does not exist -- the real Intel XPU directory is `modelserver/xpu/vllm/`.

### My understanding of the cause (please double-check before merging)

Based on reading `llm-d-benchmark`'s kustomize README parser (`llmdbenchmark/kustomize/...`) and comparing CI run history around commit `af774dc6`, it looks like:

- The parser extracts every `kubectl apply -k ...` line from this guide's "Deploy the Model Server" section into an ordered list, and selects the first one whose *resolved* path contains the requested accelerator backend. Its accelerator-rewrite step (from what I can tell) does a plain substring replace of `modelserver/gpu/vllm`.
- Since the GPU overlay directory is named `modelserver/gpu/vllm-deepseek-r1-0528`, and that name still starts with the literal substring `modelserver/gpu/vllm`, resolving the GPU command for the `xpu` backend appears to mangle it into `modelserver/xpu/vllm-deepseek-r1-0528` -- which then also matches the "does this contain `modelserver/xpu/vllm`" check used for selection. Because the GPU command currently appears before the Intel XPU command in this README, the parser seems to pick the mangled GPU command instead of the correct XPU one.

I have **not** reproduced this by actually running the `llm-d-benchmark` tool locally against both orderings, so treat this as my best-effort read of the code rather than a confirmed root cause -- happy to be corrected if a maintainer with more context sees it differently.

### Proposed fix

Reorder the Intel XPU deploy command ahead of the NVIDIA GPU one in the "Deploy the Model Server" section, splitting them into their own fenced code blocks (matching the style already used in the Router section of this same guide). The Cleanup section's two `kubectl delete` lines are also reordered the same way for consistency, but left in a single shared fence (not split), since the teardown step runs every parsed cleanup command regardless of order anyway. If my understanding above is correct, the deploy-side reorder should make the parser's selection logic land on the real XPU command; if not, please push back.

This is a documentation-only reordering -- the actual `kubectl` commands and paths are unchanged, so manual/human usage of the guide is unaffected either way.

## Verification

- Grepped `guides/*/README.md` for the same GPU/XPU-combined-command pattern; didn't find another guide using a model-suffixed backend directory name that collides with the `gpu/vllm` / `xpu/vllm` prefix convention, so this looks like an isolated case, but I haven't exhaustively audited every guide.
- Diff is a pure reorder + code-fence split; no command/path text changed.

title: CI: extract duplicated guide rendering into scripts/render.sh
body:
## Problem

`ci-kustomize-dry-run.yaml` encodes "how to hydrate a guide" inline, repeatedly:

- The router helm values layering (`base.values.yaml` + features + guide values) is copy-pasted **three times**, once per guide job, each hardcoding chart names, versions, and release names.
- `kustomize build` is invoked from **four differently-shaped loops**.

Every new guide job grows the workflow by another copy, and each copy must be kept in sync with the guide READMEs by hand. Small inconsistencies already exist between the copies (whether the monitoring layer is included, release naming conventions), which is the expected failure mode of this structure.

## What this PR does

Extracts the render commands into `scripts/render.sh` and refactors the workflow to call it. **Scope is deliberately minimal:**

- The workflow keeps its own overlay discovery loops, CRD install steps, per-unit pass/fail accounting, and `kubectl apply --dry-run=server`. Only the `helm template` / `kustomize build` lines are replaced.
- Deliberately preserved as-is (each is a candidate for its own follow-up, not silently changed here): the dev chart channel (`llm-d-router-*-dev` at `v0`), the existing release names (`optimized-baseline-router`, `pd-disaggregation-router`), and the existing per-job overlay discovery globs.
- Cleanups: removes the dead `simulated-accelerators` filter (no job, no output, no such guide directory), adds `scripts/render.sh` + `guides/env.sh` to the path filters, and extends shellcheck pre-commit coverage to the new script.

## Why this cannot break CI

The script's stdout carries only manifests (all logging goes to stderr), so `render.sh ... > /tmp/rendered.yaml` is a drop-in for the old commands. Verified locally:

- **Router units (5/5 byte-identical):** for each router render the workflow performs (optimized-baseline standalone + gateway, pd-disaggregation standalone + gateway, precise-prefix-cache-routing standalone), ran the old inline `helm template` and the new `render.sh` invocation back-to-back and diffed: empty. A control run (old command twice) confirmed template determinism against the floating `v0` tag first.
- **Overlays (18/18 byte-identical):** enumerated exactly the overlay set the workflow builds today using the workflow's own globs/find, diffed `kustomize build` against `render.sh overlay` for each: empty. `render.sh overlay <dir>` runs the same `kustomize build <dir>` underneath.
- shellcheck (`-x --severity=warning`, same as the hook) and yamllint (repo config) are clean.
- This PR touches the workflow file itself, which is in every path filter, so **all four dry-run jobs execute against this change** - a green run here is direct end-to-end evidence.

## Follow-ups this unlocks (separate PRs)

With rendering centralized, the workflow can be improved incrementally:

1. **Rendered-manifest diff in the job summary**: render base and head refs, publish the hydrated diff to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`, so a one-line values change shows its full blast radius at review time (no extra permissions needed).
2. **Close the overlay coverage gap**: the existing 2-level globs in the optimized-baseline and pd-disaggregation jobs skip overlays whose kustomization sits at depth 3 (`gpu/vllm/base`, `gpu/*/gke`, `tpu/*`), so the default GPU paths are not currently dry-run. `render.sh list <guide>` already discovers these correctly (recursive, excludes kustomize components); switching the loops over is a small, reviewable change once any newly-surfaced failures are addressed.
3. **Revisit dev vs release chart validation**: CI validates the `-dev` charts at `v0` while the READMEs deploy release charts at `ROUTER_CHART_VERSION` - worth deciding whether CI should (also) validate what users actually install.

## Add-on: usable outside CI

Because the script encodes the same layering the READMEs document, it doubles as an inspection tool for users who want to see the full hydrated stack of a guide before or instead of deploying with helm:

```bash
# full stack for pd-disaggregation on GPU + GKE, standalone router
scripts/render.sh all pd-disaggregation --modelserver gpu/vllm/gke -o rendered/
```

Output defaults to release charts pinned in `guides/env.sh` (what the READMEs install); `--dev` selects the dev channel CI validates.

title: Make DisaggregatedSet the base for the wide-EP GLM-5.2 guide
body:
## What

Converts the wide-EP GLM-5.2 guide to `DisaggregatedSet`, following #2379.

- One DS with prefill and decode roles replaces the LWS prefill/decode manifests.
- Role `rolloutStrategy` pinned to maxSurge 0, maxUnavailable 1 to match the old LWS defaults.
- The coreweave provider and the components patch env, volumes, and containers by name via a DS schema declared once in the base, with shared role specs written once via YAML anchors.
- The 27 deployments only set replicas and group size, so they use JSON6902 against the fixed [prefill, decode] role order.

Name-based patching also fixes a bug: the old no-mtp patch replaced env index 5, which was KV_OFFLOAD_CPU_BYTES on prefill and ENABLE_PROFILING on decode, and left a duplicate ENABLE_MTP where the last entry ("1") wins. So the baseline and offloading benchmark overlays never actually disabled MTP. It now sets a single ENABLE_MTP=0 and keeps those vars.

All 30 kustomizations render semantically identical to the LWS manifests they replace, except the pinned rolloutStrategy, the `llm-d.ai/inference-serving` role label, and the no-mtp fix in the 9 overlays that use it.

title: Guarantee a scale-from-zero path in the fast-model-actuation-keda verification
body:
## Summary
The verification request could hit an already-warm pool. The guide now stands up at
the `ScaledObject` floor of 1, waits for KEDA to scale it to zero, then sends the test
request from there.

- **`keda/base/`**: `cooldownPeriod` and the HPA's `scaleDown.stabilizationWindowSeconds`
  300s → 30s each — they apply sequentially, so both must be cut; scale-to-zero now
  takes ~1 min instead of ~10. This guide's overlay only; the upstream base keeps its
  production values.
- **Step 6**: new wait for `spec.replicas == 0`. That is what proves the metric pipeline
  works — `Ready` only means KEDA accepted the trigger.
- **Step 2**: one request at `--max-time 600` instead of a 12×15s retry loop — flow
  control holds it through the whole 0→1 transition. Now also checks HTTP status: the
  old form had no `--fail`, and `set -e` misses a curl failure inside a pipeline, so a
  non-200 or a timeout could pass.
- **Prose**: notes the scale-up should be a **hot start** and links the numbers (4.0 s
  vs 85.3 s pod startup, `Qwen/Qwen3-32B`), with the GPU-assignment caveat deferred to
  the FMA guide.

title: feat(sglang): add sglang-decode-hicache component for P/D disaggregation
body:
## What this changes

Adds an opt-in Kustomize component `guides/pd-disaggregation/modelserver/components/sglang-decode-hicache` that enables decode-side prefix caching with a host-DRAM (L2) tier for SGLang P/D disaggregation by layering it over any provider overlay:

```yaml
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization
resources:
  - guides/pd-disaggregation/modelserver/gpu/sglang/gke  # or base | coreweave | aws
components:
  - guides/pd-disaggregation/modelserver/components/sglang-decode-hicache
```

When included, the component configures:
- `--disaggregation-decode-enable-radix-cache`: SGLang forces `disable_radix_cache=True` on decode servers in P/D mode unless this flag is passed. Without it, a decode pod keeps no prefix state and every turn of a conversation re-transfers its whole prefix from prefill.
- `--enable-hierarchical-cache`: adds a host-DRAM tier beneath HBM.
- `--hicache-size=64`: sets the host KV pool to 64 GB per TP rank (128 GB per pod at TP=2).
- `requests.memory: 256Gi` and `limits.memory: 256Gi`: reserves the host pool upfront to prevent node memory overcommit (eliminating cgroup OOMs on high-HBM cards like H200/B200) and protects against kubelet memory-pressure eviction ranking (the container cannot exceed its request), while providing ~128 GB headroom above the pinned host pool for model weights, engine runtime, and the 16Gi `/dev/shm` tmpfs. On an 8-GPU node with 4 TP=2 pods, 4 × 256Gi = 1,024 GiB (≤55% of node RAM on `a3-megagpu-8g` or `p5.48xlarge`), so GPUs remain the binding constraint without orphaning memory.

The base manifests and provider overlays (`base`, `aws`, `coreweave`, `gke`) remain completely untouched and default to standard P/D serving without prefix caching.

## Results

2× prefill + 2× decode, all TP=2, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, ~12k-token prompts, TTFT p50, on GKE with 4× `a3-megagpu-8g` (NVIDIA H100 Mega 80GB). Routing is **pinned, not observed** — the decode replica is addressed through its routing-proxy sidecar and prefill is pinned with `x-prefiller-host-port` — so prefill-side caching is held constant:

| | before | **after** |
|---|---|---|
| turn 1 (cold) | 1.247 s | 1.271 s |
| turn 2, replica holding the prefix | 1.235 s | **0.262 s** |
| turn 2, a different decode replica | 1.258 s | 1.203 s |

Flushing the prefill radix cache too (forcing full prefill recompute), turn 2 on the replica holding the prefix goes 1.372 s → **0.417 s** (3.3× win). The baseline is not a strawman: on turn 2 prefill reported `#cached-token: 12032` of 12160 (~99% hit) and TTFT barely moved — prefill caching is not the lever, avoiding decode-side KV transfer is.

Stability: 4 clean runs in this configuration, 0 crashes and 0 restarts.

## Routing and Incompatibilities

- **Replica-local**: the router's decode scheduling profile selects the least-busy pod without prefix-cache affinity (unlike the prefill profile, which has affinity). A follow-up turn hits the warm decode replica only when scheduled there; otherwise behavior matches the pre-change baseline.
- **Incompatibilities**: SGLang's decode radix cache currently conflicts with speculative decoding (`--speculative-algorithm`), `--enable-hisparse`, and `--disaggregation-transfer-backend fake`. Keeping this as an opt-in component ensures `base/` remains compatible with speculative decoding.

## Note on L3 (shared filesystem offload)

A shared `ReadWriteMany` L3 tier (`--hicache-storage-backend file`) was also implemented and benchmarked, and is **not** included here. In P/D disaggregation, the alternative to reading a prefix from shared storage is re-transferring KV from a prefill pod rather than recomputing prefill (~0.17 s for 12k tokens). Shared storage must beat the P/D interconnect rather than GPU compute, which is generally disadvantageous.

title: docs: add multi-endpoint serving guide
body:
**What type of PR is this?**
/kind documentation

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Adds a multi-endpoint serving guide under the existing `diffusion-serving` package, consolidating single-endpoint and multi-endpoint deployment patterns in one place per reviewer feedback.

The multi-endpoint guide deploys a single model that serves **multiple modality endpoints** from one checkpoint (e.g. Qwen3-Omni serving text, audio, and images), using a single Gateway API HTTPRoute with multiple exact-path match rules to direct each endpoint to the model's InferencePool.

**Architecture:**

```
/v1/audio/speech         (Exact) → model-pool → model pods  (if model supports TTS)
/v1/audio/transcriptions (Exact) → model-pool → model pods  (if model supports ASR)
/v1/images/generations   (Exact) → model-pool → model pods  (if model supports image gen)
/v1/chat/completions             → catch-all  → model-pool  (or text pool)
```

The EPP uses the standard config (`queue-scorer` + `max-score-picker`, no custom plugins). Pod homogeneity within the pool eliminates the need for architecture-aware filtering.

**This PR includes:**

- `guides/diffusion-serving/multi-endpoint/README.md` — guide covering multi-endpoint deployment with architecture, model capability table, prerequisites, installation, verification per modality, multi-pool deployment, and cleanup
- `guides/diffusion-serving/multi-endpoint/httproutes.yaml` — single HTTPRoute with multiple exact-path match rules for all supported modality endpoints
- `guides/diffusion-serving/multi-endpoint/router/values.yaml` — Helm values for standard EPP config
- `guides/diffusion-serving/multi-endpoint/modelserver/gpu/vllmomni/base/` — Kustomize overlay and deployment patch for vLLM-Omni model server (default: Qwen3-Omni)
- `guides/diffusion-serving/README.md` — updated with single-endpoint and multi-endpoint sections

**Changes from review feedback:**

- Consolidated under `diffusion-serving/` instead of a separate `omni-serving/` package
- Simplified HTTPRoutes into a single resource with multiple path matches (was 3 separate HTTPRoute objects)
- Simplified values.yaml plugin config (removed explicit plugin names)

**Validation:**

- Validated the separate InferencePool + HTTPRoute routing architecture on OpenShift (wetlab-ai) with separate pools, each with its own EPP running standard config. Both EPPs healthy, caches populated, pools reconciled, HTTPRoutes accepted by Gateway.
- Kustomize build passes for the new overlay.

title: fix(scripts): lint-envvars.py always exited 0, silently disabling the pre-commit/CI gate
body:
## Summary

`scripts/lint-envvars.py` — the env-var declaration linter documented in `scripts/ENVVARS.md` and enforced via `.pre-commit-config.yaml` / the CI `pre-commit` job — has never actually failed a build. `main()` prints its findings but then unconditionally calls `sys.exit(0)`:

```python
if all_errors:
    for error in all_errors:
        print(error, file=sys.stderr)
    print(f"\n⚠ {len(all_errors)} warning(s) found", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(0)          # <-- always succeeds, even with errors
```

Its sibling `lint-dockerfile-envvars.py` already exits 1 on failure, and `ENVVARS.md` describes this as an enforced check ("The `lint-envvars.py` tool enforces this at lint time"), not an opt-in warning — so this is a bug, not a deliberate "warn only" design.

## What flipping it on surfaces

Turning the exit code into a real gate immediately exposed two more issues, both fixed in this PR so the newly-real gate is green from the start:

1. **A detection false-negative in the linter itself**: `find_locally_defined_vars` only matched assignments anchored at the very start of a line, so a `case` arm one-liner like
   ```bash
   linux/arm64) export SCCACHE_SERVER_UDS="..." ;;
   ```
   was never recognized as a local definition, producing a false "undeclared variable" report on `setup-sccache.sh`. Fixed by also matching assignments right after a `)`.

2. **Real, pre-existing undeclared vars** across `docker/scripts/**` that had been accumulating silently since the check never actually failed anything:
   - `build-uccl.sh`: `TARGETOS`, `VIRTUAL_ENV` — used, never declared
   - `build-nixl.sh`, `build-nvshmem.sh`, `build-ucx.sh`: `MAX_JOBS` — used to parallelize the build, never declared
   - `install-vllm.sh`: `CUDA_MINOR`, `FLASHINFER_VERSION`, `NVSHMEM_BUILD_FROM_SOURCE`, `VLLM_CHERRYPICK_1`/`_REMOTE`, `VLLM_CHERRYPICK_2`/`_REMOTE`, `VLLM_SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION` (the last is only referenced by a currently commented-out `export`; documented rather than removed since it looks intended for future re-enablement)

These are documentation-only additions to each script's existing "Required/Optional environment variables" header — no runtime behavior changes.

## Note for maintainers

Fixing the exit code also exposed that `docker/Dockerfile.rocm` currently fails the *sibling* `lint-dockerfile-envvars.py` check (missing `UCCL_DEVICE`/`UCCL_PREFIX` ARG/ENV declarations for `build-uccl.sh`). That's pre-existing and reproducible on `main` today, independent of this PR — I left it out of scope since it's a GPU-specific Dockerfile I can't build/test locally. Happy to file a follow-up issue if useful.

## Testing
- `python3 scripts/lint-envvars.py $(git ls-files 'docker/scripts/**/*.sh')` now exits 0 across the whole tree (previously always exited 0 regardless of content, which is exactly the bug).
- Manually reverted the exit-code fix locally to confirm the same command now correctly exits 1 when a script has an undeclared var.
