docs(router): drop monitoring values from the agentgateway install command
body:
Follow-up to #2134 / #2138. Fixes #2322.

`guides/recipes/router/README.md` has three `helm install` commands. #2138 removed
`features/monitoring.values.yaml` from **Standalone with Envoy** and **With Kubernetes
Gateway API**, and missed the third — **Standalone with agentgateway** — which still
carried it. That block already had the flag at `709a67e2^` (added in #1719), so this is
a miss rather than a later regression.

## Why it still failed

Nothing in the agentgateway path suppresses the `ServiceMonitor`:
`features/agentgateway-proxy.values.yaml` only overrides `router.proxy.args`, and
`features/monitoring.values.yaml` still sets `router.monitoring.prometheus.enabled: true`.

Rendering the documented command against the published chart, before this change:

```
$ helm template test oci://ghcr.io/llm-d/charts/llm-d-router-standalone --version v0 \
    -f base.values.yaml -f monitoring.values.yaml -f agentgateway-proxy.values.yaml \
    --set router.proxy.proxyType=agentgateway \
    --set router.inferencePool.create=false \
    --set router.epp.flags.secure-serving=false \
    --set router.modelServers.matchLabels.app=demo -n testns | grep -E '^kind:|^apiVersion: monitoring'

apiVersion: monitoring.coreos.com/v1
kind: ServiceMonitor
```

So on a cluster without the Prometheus Operator CRDs the whole install aborts with the
`no matches for kind "ServiceMonitor"` error from #2134. After this change the same
render emits no `ServiceMonitor`.

## Second change

The **Enable Prometheus Monitoring (Optional)** section tells the reader to layer
monitoring onto an existing release with `helm upgrade`, but its command carries neither
`agentgateway-proxy.values.yaml` nor the three `--set` flags. Since `helm upgrade` does
not inherit the previous release's values, an agentgateway user following it would revert
their proxy configuration to chart defaults. Removing the flag from the install command
without saying this would just move the trap, so I added a `NOTE` to that section.

## Not addressed here

The agentgateway command also cannot be templated as written:

```
Error: execution error at (llm-d-router-standalone/templates/epp.yaml:2:3):
.Values.router.modelServers.matchLabels is required when
.Values.router.inferencePool.create=false
```

`router.inferencePool.create=false` is required for agentgateway (the README's own `NOTE`
says so), and the chart then requires `router.modelServers.matchLabels`, which neither the
command nor the surrounding text mentions. Presumably it is meant to come from
`<your-guide>.values.yaml`, but that is not stated. Left out to keep this reviewable —
happy to fold it in or file it separately.

body:
Closes #1713

## what this does

the llm-d-router-standalone chart already supports agentgateway as a sidecar proxy (`router.proxy.proxyType=agentgateway`) but none of the guides mentioned it, everything just assumed envoy. this PR adds the agentgateway docs and lines up the install commands with the chart's pseudo-service model (no service.name/service.ports needed anymore).

## changes

**guides/recipes/router/README.md**
- new "Standalone with agentgateway" section next to the existing envoy one, with a working helm install example
- NOTE callout for the required flags (`inferencePool.create=false`, `epp.flags.secure-serving=false`)
- added a Prerequisites section for the env vars used across these guides (REPO_ROOT, NAMESPACE, ROUTER_CHART_VERSION, via guides/env.sh)

**guides/recipes/router/base.values.yaml**
- kept the explicit envoy args here instead of switching to `args: []`. tried that first but the chart preset uses `--cpuset-threads` instead of `--concurrency 8`, and since this pod has no cpu limit that ends up spawning threads off the whole node instead of the tuned value from the v0.8.0 benchmark run. so args stayed as is, agentgateway gets its own args from the features overlay below

**guides/recipes/router/features/agentgateway-proxy.values.yaml** (new)
- sets proxyType: agentgateway + the required flags, swaps out the envoy args for agentgateway's

**guides/optimized-baseline/README.md**
- just points to the router recipes guide for agentgateway now instead of duplicating a whole snippet here, didn't want to add another dimension to an already complex guide

**docs/api-reference/artifacts.md**
- updated the standalone chart description to mention agentgateway as an option

## testing

ran `helm template` against both proxyType=envoy and proxyType=agentgateway for the affected guides.

also did a real e2e run on a fresh kind cluster, not just template. ran the exact helm install commands from `guides/recipes/router/README.md` for both paths:
- standalone with envoy: pod came up 2/2 running, sent a real `/v1/completions` request, got a real completion back
- standalone with agentgateway: same, pod 2/2 running, real completion back

only deviations from the literal guide commands were cpu/memory resource overrides (the guide's defaults are 4 cpu / 8gi per component, meant for real clusters, too big for a kind node) and the agentgateway image tag override, since the chart's built-in default tag doesn't exist in the registry. everything else ran exactly as documented.

## related

title: Set tags on `main` branch back to "main"
Match llm-d.ai/model-id to the served model name
body:
## Summary

The WVA guide annotates its ScaledObject and HPA with `llm-d.ai/model-id: "Qwen3-32B"`, but the model server it ships runs `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-32B` with no `--served-model-name`, so vLLM labels its metrics `model_name="Qwen/Qwen3-32B"`. WVA matches that label exactly, so every saturation query returns zero series.

This corrects the annotation in both autoscaling paths to the served model name.

## Why it matters

The failure mode is silent and looks entirely healthy. WVA logs:

```
No saturation metrics available for model, skipping analysis {"modelID": "Qwen3-32B", ...}
Optimization completed successfully {"mode": "saturation", "modelsProcessed": 1, "decisionsApplied": 0}
```

It then publishes `wva_desired_replicas` equal to the *current* replica count, so KEDA consumes a real series and never falls back. The ScaledObject reports `Ready=True`, `Active=True`, `Fallback=False`, the HPA tracks its target, and the stack passes every health check — while the autoscaler is inert and the replica count only ever echoes itself.

Because `Fallback=False` holds either way, the usual smoke test cannot distinguish a working autoscaler from this one.

## Test plan

Verified end to end on a MI355X cluster running the guide's own stack (2 replicas, TP2, KEDA 2.20.1, kube-prometheus-stack over TLS).

With the shipped annotation, across every 15 s optimization cycle:

```
Processing model (V2)  {"modelID": "Qwen3-32B", ...}
No saturation metrics available for model, skipping analysis
EmitReplicaMetrics completed  {"currentReplicas": 2, "desiredReplicas": 2, ...}
```

Correcting only this annotation, with nothing else changed:

```
Processing model (V2)  {"modelID": "Qwen/Qwen3-32B", ...}
EmitReplicaMetrics completed  {"currentReplicas": 2, "desiredReplicas": 1, "accelerator": "MI355X"}
Optimization completed successfully  {"mode": "saturation", "modelsProcessed": 1, "decisionsApplied": 1}
```

`desiredReplicas: 1` against 2 running is the correct call for an idle deployment, and the HPA target moved to `500m/1 (avg)` accordingly.

Queried directly against Prometheus, `Qwen3-32B` returns 0 series and `Qwen/Qwen3-32B` returns the live `vllm:` series the saturation thresholds read.

## Note

Reaching real decisions also requires the `vllm:` series to exist at all, and neither optimized-baseline model server base includes `recipes/modelserver/components/monitoring`. That is a separate gap and I will open an issue for it; this change is necessary regardless, since correcting the scrape alone still leaves every query unmatched.

title: doc(guides): Introduce standardized recipes for Gateway, InferencePool, and vLLM
body:
This change introduces 
1. a set of reusable and standardized recipes under guides/recipes to simplify the
process of creating new deployment guides. Following: #405
2. It also refactors the CPU Prefix Cache guide to be the first consumer of these new components.



Key changes include:

   * Standardized Naming: Established a consistent naming convention for core components:
       * Gateway: `llm-d-inference-gateway`
       * HTTPRoute: `llm-d-route`
       * InferencePool: `llm-d-infpool`
   * Standardized Labeling: The label `llm-d.ai/inferenceServing: "true"` is now used consistently on model
     server deployments and is the default selector for the InferencePool recipe.
   * Reusable Recipes: Created modular recipes for:
       * Gateway: A base gateway and a GKE-specific overlay.
       * InferencePool: A standard `values.yaml` for the Helm chart.
       * vLLM: A base deployment that can be easily customized.
   * Improved Documentation: Each recipe includes a `README.md` with clear installation and verification
     instructions.
   * Refactored Guide: The `guides/prefix-cache-storage/cpu` guide has been updated to use these new
     recipes, making it much simpler and easier to follow.

title: ci: restore bespoke flow-control nightly e2e
body:
**Problem**

The flow-control nightly e2e has failed every scheduled run since #1728 merged. Two hours after #1728 landed, a fleet-wide normalization to the benchmark harness (#1766) moved flow-control into `reusable-ci-nightly-benchmark.yaml` and deleted the bespoke `custom_deploy_script` and `--extra-validate` handoff. The bespoke e2e never reached a scheduled run.

The benchmark harness cannot stand the guide up. Its kustomize standup detects the model from `guides/<scenario>/modelserver/<accel>/<backend>/<infra>/`. The flow-control guide keeps no `modelserver/` overlay and borrows optimized-baseline's, which is what the guide README tells users to do. Runs fail at standup with `unable to detect model`. `reusable-ci-nightly-benchmark.yaml` carries a flow-control special case that borrows the optimized-baseline overlay, but it runs after the model-detection step that needs the missing directory, so it never executes. Filing that against the harness separately.

A benchmark run would also leave the feature untested. Flow control is work-conserving, so `sanity_random` never produces queue contention. Backpressure, per-band isolation, and QoS ordering go unexercised.

`workload-autoscaling` runs a bespoke lane for the same missing-overlay reason.

**Change**

Point the `nightly` job at `reusable-nightly-e2e-gke.yaml` with `e2e_validate_args: '--extra-validate flow-control'`. Move the deploy logic into `guides/flow-control/scripts/nightly-deploy-gke.sh`, following the workload-autoscaling precedent, which also picks up shellcheck via `ci-pr-checks`.

The script follows the guide README's install steps. It carries three CI-only deviations, each marked inline: a low `maxConcurrency` so the saturation gate closes under the validate script's burst, `prometheus.auth.enabled=false` so the validate pod can scrape `/metrics`, and the optimized-baseline modelserver relabel the README already documents.

`reusable-nightly-e2e-gke.yaml` declares no outputs, so `failure_category` resolves empty and the badge falls back to plain pass/fail. The workload-autoscaling lanes behave the same way.

**Fixes since the last review**

- `/test-nightly` could not dispatch the lane, which is why no green run has ever existed. `slash-test-nightly.yaml` sends its `DEFAULT_PARAMS` to every `nightly-e2e-*` workflow whether or not the caller passes any, and its 422 fallback retries only without `pr_number` and `pr_repo`. One undeclared parameter therefore fails both attempts. The workflow now declares all of them as accepted no-ops, matching workload-autoscaling, with a comment tying the set to `SUPPORTED_PARAMS`.
- Merge conflict with #1951 over the `update_badge` input and the `if:` gate on the badge job. Resolved with both kept.
- Cron moved from 15:00 UTC to 17:00 UTC, since `pd-disaggregation-gke-sglang` took 15:30. The job is gated on `github.repository == 'llm-d/llm-d'` so forks do not schedule it.
- Merged `main` to pick up #2209 (see Testing) and dropped the script's local CRD version pin in favor of `ROUTER_RELEASE_VERSION`, which #2209 added to `guides/env.sh`.

**Scope**

The lane covers priority ordering. Weighted multi-tenant fairness and SLO attainment at scale need inference-perf multi-tenant trace replay, which is not available yet. The guide's Benchmarking section describes that heavier tier.

No source or library changes.

**Testing**

The first dispatched run ([31821164596](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/actions/runs/31821164596)) failed at standup. `guides/flow-control/router/flow-control.values.yaml` declared a `metrics: 9090` Service port on top of the chart's built-in `http-metrics: 9090`, so the EPP Service failed admission:

```
Service "flow-control-epp" is invalid: spec.ports[3]: Duplicate value: {Port: 9090}
```

#2209 removed the duplicate entry. #2209 also changed the `objectives.yaml` `poolRef` from `default-pool` to `flow-control`; without that change the InferenceObjectives bind nothing, tagged traffic falls back to band 0, and the per-band assertions report on an empty pool. Both fixes come in with the `main` merge.

A green on-demand run is still required before merge: `/test-nightly flow-control-gke-acc-gpu-vllm-x`. No step after standup has executed yet, including the validate script and its backpressure assertions.

**Motivation**

Flow control remains opt-in at GA (llm-d-router#2180). Coverage of flow-control behavior comes only from the flow-control lane: backpressure, per-band isolation, and priority QoS. The other guides' lanes report whether their guide still stands up.

title: fix(workload-autoscaling): remove obsolete CRD step
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

/kind bug
/kind cleanup

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

The WVA guide's CRD install step is broken on `main`. `wva/guide.yaml`'s `crds:` step runs `kubectl apply -k .../config/base/crd?ref=main`, but that path no longer exists in the WVA repo: the `VariantAutoscaling` CRD was removed in v0.9 (no `api/` type, `make manifests` generates only RBAC + webhook, and there is no `config/base/crd` dir on `main` or `release-0.9`). WVA is now annotation-based — you annotate an existing HPA/KEDA ScaledObject — so there is no CRD to install and the step fails for anyone running the guide. This also pins the guide to the release branch ahead of the llm-d release.

- Remove the `crds:` step from `wva/guide.yaml` and its rendered `guide:deploy.crds` block from `wva/README.md`; renumber the following deploy steps. README re-rendered with `scripts/guide.py render`.

Verification:
- `scripts/guide.py render guides/workload-autoscaling/wva --check` reports the README up to date.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:

N/A — surfaced during WVA v0.9 release prep; no separate tracking issue.

**Release note**:

```release-note
The workload-variant-autoscaler guide no longer installs the removed VariantAutoscaling CRD (WVA is annotation-based as of v0.9)
```

title: docs(flow-control): make use-case verification observable and fix guide friction
body:
The Use Case 2 load test could not demonstrate the queuing it claims to verify, and an audit of the rest of the guide surfaced more breakage in the same file. Every changed command was validated on a live cluster (GKE, Helm 4.2.0, one Qwen3-32B TP=2 replica).

## Use Case 2

- Replace the dead `hey` download (S3 returns 403; the debug image's busybox wget lacks TLS) with a curl loop using tools already in the debug image.
- Sustain the load so the queue is observable: `max_tokens: 500`, `ignore_eos: true`, ~2k-token prompt; burst in the background and poll while it runs. The old payload drained in under a second.
- Derive the test sizing from the values file instead of hardcoding it. `MAX_CONCURRENCY` is read out of `router/flow-control.values.yaml` with awk and passed into the debug pod; the burst is `MAX_CONCURRENCY + SURPLUS` and the expected queue peak is `SURPLUS` (20, kept below the best-effort band's `maxRequests`). A retuned values file changes the test with it, so the guide's numbers cannot drift out from under the config.
- Scale the pool to one replica for the burst, recording the prior replica count and restoring it afterward rather than assuming 8.
- Pre-flight a single request (expect 200) before the burst; sum all `priority="-10"` series in the poll; the peak-0 diagnosis covers poll timing and replica count.

## Rest of the guide

- Use Case 1: add a verification step; `llm_d_epp_flow_control_request_queue_duration_seconds_count` must show a `priority="100"` series (records on every outcome, including immediate dispatch).
- `helm install` → `helm upgrade --install` in both install commands; the re-run instructions already assumed it.
- Add `-c epp` to the verification grep as an in-block comment; kubectl defaults to the Envoy sidecar, whose log never matches.
- Pass `MODEL_NAME` into the debug pod; the UC1 request body and UC2 payload use it in-pod.
- Document the router pod's 8 vCPU / 16 GiB request at the install step, citing `base.values.yaml` as the source.
- Drop the stale `[Experimental]` title, a duplicate QoS caveat, and the hardcoded `--model` value.

## helpers/benchmark.md

Harness- and provider-specific material moved to the benchmarking helper (the declared single source of truth for benchmarking), which the guide now links instead of duplicating:

- New troubleshooting entry for `ProvisioningFailed ... multi writer with mount access type`: the RWX StorageClass requirement, the `storage.workloadPvc.storageClassName` scenario override, a GKE Filestore walkthrough, and stale-claim recovery (PVC StorageClass is immutable and the CLI reuses an existing claim).
- New troubleshooting entry for the harness pod stuck `Pending` on its 16 vCPU / 32 GiB request.
- New "Cleaning up harness resources" section; the guide's Cleanup links it. The workload PVC is backed by shared storage that bills until removed.
- The guide's benchmark section keeps a single NOTE pointing at both.

Follow-up: a `llmdbenchmark cleanup` subcommand upstream would replace the hand-maintained resource list in benchmark.md entirely; issue to be filed on llm-d/llm-d-benchmark.

## Observed on the live run

- UC1: `outcome="Dispatched", priority="100"` count 1 after one premium request.
- UC2 (pre-parameterization commands): peak queue depth 18 from a 150-request burst against `maxConcurrency` 132 — the same arithmetic the derived commands now encode with `SURPLUS=20` (expected peak 20). <!-- update after re-running UC2 with the derived sizing -->
- Benchmark: the documented GKE failure mode reproduces; with the StorageClass override on a fresh claim, Filestore bound in ~2.5 min and `shared_prefix_synthetic.yaml` ran end to end.
- Not covered on a 2-GPU cluster: detector behavior while ready endpoints drain, 8-replica scale-back timing.

title: Fix oneCCL init failure for tiered-prefix-cache on Intel XPU
body:
The XPU decode pod crash-looped during standup with:
  oneCCL: atl_ofi_comm.cpp:232 init_transport: EXCEPTION: failed to initialize ATL
  CCL_ERROR| atl_ofi_helper.cpp:1118 fi_getinfo error: ret -61, providers 0

With tensor-parallel-size=4 the vLLM XPU worker initializes the xccl/oneCCL backend, which defaults to the OFI transport. The bundled libfabric in the container exposes no providers because FI_PROVIDER_PATH is unset, so ATL initialization fails and the engine core never starts.

Point libfabric at the Intel MPI provider directory shipped in the image and select the tcp provider. Verified on a kind cluster with Intel XPUs: the decode pod now reaches Ready with tensor-parallel-size=4 and the OffloadingConnector.
